newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asahi sees share of Japan beer market bubbling up.
newsitem.headline: Asahi sees share of Japan beer market bubbling up.

text.p: Japan's second-biggest beer maker Asahi Breweries Ltd sees its share of the domestic market bubbling up to 35 percent by the end of this year.
Asahi also hopes to boost overseas sales, currently accounting for just one percent of overall sales, to at least 10 percent, president Yuzo Seto told Reuters in an interview.
It hopes to do so by strengthening its business in China, he said. Asahi is also reviewing its relationship with Foster's Brewing Group Ltd of Australia, he added.
"Our beer shipments in the January-May period were 13 percent larger than those of last year, which is outstanding compared with the industry's average of a two percent fall," Seto said.

"Our (domestic) shipments will reach 35 percent of total domestic shipments this year," he said, adding that Asahi's domestic shipments had increased to more than 34 percent of the total in the January-May period.
Japan's biggest beer maker is Kirin Brewery Co Ltd, which captured 46.6 percent of the domestic market in 1996.
But Kirin's market share in 1996 was down 2.3 percentage points from 1995, while Asahi's share was up 3.2 percentage points from the previous year at 30.4 percent in 1996.
"The reason for our growth is Super Dry beer. Sales have steadily increased since it was launched 10 years ago, and have accelerated since the second half of last year," Seto said.

Seto said he hopes to strengthen production in China, where the company already produces beer at five plants, to three million cases this year and five million cases in 1998, up from 1.6 million cases in 1996.
Asahi started production of Super Dry in China in April.
Seto also said Asahi would make a decision soon on its relationship with Foster's, in which it has a 14 percent stake.
The future relationship would be a "completely new one", he said, but he did not elaborate.
Asahi also plans total capital investment of 80 billion yen ($689 million) for calendar 1997, Seto said.
Of that, 65 billion yen ($560 million) will be used for production facilities, 2.7 times larger than in 1996, he said.
Seto said he now expected parent sales and current profit for the 1997 business year, which started on January 1, to be larger than the company forecast in February.

But he added that while sales were expected to be larger than forecast, current profit would not be much larger than predicted in February because Asahi planned to include losses on securities holdings in its 1997 earnings.

In February, Asahi said its 1997 parent current profit would be 30 billion yen ($258 million), against 25.72 billion yen ($221 million) in 1996, on expected sales of 950 billion yen ($8.18 billion), against 931.20 billion yen ($8.02 billion).
Seto said Asahi plans to reduce its debts to less than 400 billion yen ($3.44 billion) by the end of 1997 from 450 billion yen ($3.87 billion) at the end of 1996.
Seto said he will seek approval at a shareholders' meeting in December for a plan to introduce a stock-option scheme for employees. ($1=116 yen)
